Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(D\) be the set of positive divisors of \(250\):
\[
D=\{1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250\}.
\]
For \(i=j\), the condition gives \(|A_i|=i\). Also, if \(d\mid e\), then
\[
|A_d\cap A_e|=\gcd(d,e)=d=|A_d|,
\]
so \(A_d\subseteq A_e\).

---

## 1. Structure of the sets \(A_d\) for \(d\mid 250\)

For \(d,e\in D\), let \(g=\gcd(d,e)\). Since \(A_g\subseteq A_d\cap A_e\) and both have size \(g\),
\[
A_d\cap A_e=A_g.
\]
By induction, for any finite \(F\subseteq D\),
\[
\bigcap_{d\in F}A_d=A_{\gcd(F)}.
\]

For each \(d\in D\), define
\[
B_d=A_d\setminus \bigcup_{\substack{e\mid d\\ e<d}} A_e.
\]
The sets \(B_d\) partition \(A_{250}\). Moreover,
\[
|A_d|=\sum_{e\mid d}|B_e|.
\]
Since \(|A_d|=d\), Möbius inversion on the divisor lattice gives
\[
|B_d|=\sum_{e\mid d}\mu\left(\frac de\right)e=\varphi(d).
\]
Thus
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
d&1&2&5&10&25&50&125&250\\ \hline
|B_d|&1&1&4&4&20&20&100&100
\end{array}
\]
Also, \(B_e\subseteq A_d\) if and only if \(e\mid d\).

---

## 2. Turning the problem into a path problem

For \(b=0,1,2,3\), set
\[
s_b=\varphi(5^b)=\varphi(2\cdot 5^b).
\]
Thus
\[
(s_0,s_1,s_2,s_3)=(1,4,20,100).
\]
Let
\[
S_0=0,\qquad S_i=\sum_{b=0}^{i-1}s_b\quad(1\le i\le 4).
\]
So
\[
(S_0,S_1,S_2,S_3,S_4)=(0,1,5,25,125).
\]

An ideal in the divisor lattice \(D\) is determined by a pair \((i,j)\) with \(0\le j\le i\le 4\): it contains
\[
1,5,\dots,5^{i-1}
\]
and
\[
2,10,\dots,2\cdot 5^{j-1}.
\]
The union of the corresponding \(A_d\)'s has size
\[
S_i+S_j,
\]
because it contains \(B_{5^b}\) for \(b<i\) and \(B_{2\cdot 5^b}\) for \(b<j\).

Now let
\[
M_d=\max A_d.
\]
List the divisors \(d_1,\dots,d_8\) so that
\[
M_{d_1}\le M_{d_2}\le \cdots \le M_{d_8},
\]
breaking ties so that every initial segment is an ideal in the divisor lattice. If the first \(k\) divisors form the ideal \((i_k,j_k)\), then their union has size \(S_{i_k}+S_{j_k}\), and all of its elements are at most \(M_{d_k}\). Hence
\[
M_{d_k}\ge S_{i_k}+S_{j_k}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250} M_d\ge \min \sum_{k=1}^8 (S_{i_k}+S_{j_k}),
\]
where the minimum is over all valid paths from \((0,0)\) to \((4,4)\), moving one step right in the \(i\)-direction or one step up in the \(j\)-direction, always keeping \(j\le i\).

---

## 3. Minimizing the path sum

At a state \((r,j)\) with \(r>j\), both moves
\[
(r,j)\to(r+1,j)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(r,j)\to(r,j+1)
\]
are available. Compare taking them in the two possible orders:

- Right then up:
\[
(S_{r+1}+S_j)+(S_{r+1}+S_{j+1}).
\]
- Up then right:
\[
(S_r+S_{j+1})+(S_{r+1}+S_{j+1}).
\]
Their difference is
\[
(s_r-s_j)>0
\]
because \(r>j\) and \(s_0<s_1<s_2<s_3\). Thus in an optimal path, whenever \(j<r\), we should move in the \(j\)-direction first.

So the optimal path is forced to be
\[
(0,0)\to(1,0)\to(1,1)\to(2,1)\to(2,2)\to(3,2)\to(3,3)\to(4,3)\to(4,4).
\]
The corresponding values of \(S_i+S_j\) are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{state} & S_i+S_j\\ \hline
(1,0)&1\\
(1,1)&2\\
(2,1)&6\\
(2,2)&10\\
(3,2)&30\\
(3,3)&50\\
(4,3)&150\\
(4,4)&250
\end{array}
\]
Their sum is
\[
1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250=499.
\]
Thus for every valid sequence,
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d\ge 499.
\]

---

## 4. Construction achieving \(499\)

For each positive integer \(m\), let \(X_m\) be a set of \(\varphi(m)\) distinct positive integers, with all \(X_m\) disjoint. Define
\[
A_i=\bigcup_{m\mid i}X_m.
\]
Then
\[
|A_i|=\sum_{m\mid i}\varphi(m)=i,
\]
and
\[
|A_i\cap A_j|
=\sum_{\substack{m\mid i\\ m\mid j}}\varphi(m)
=\sum_{m\mid \gcd(i,j)}\varphi(m)
=\gcd(i,j).
\]
So this gives a valid sequence.

Now assign labels to the blocks dividing \(250\) as follows:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
X_m & \text{labels}\\ \hline
X_1 & \{1\}\\
X_2 & \{2\}\\
X_5 & \{3,4,5,6\}\\
X_{10} & \{7,8,9,10\}\\
X_{25} & \{11,\dots,30\}\\
X_{50} & \{31,\dots,50\}\\
X_{125} & \{51,\dots,150\}\\
X_{250} & \{151,\dots,250\}
\end{array}
\]
For all other \(m\), choose \(X_m\) using integers larger than \(250\).

Then the relevant maxima are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\max A_1&=1,\\
\max A_2&=2,\\
\max A_5&=6,\\
\max A_{10}&=10,\\
\max A_{25}&=30,\\
\max A_{50}&=50,\\
\max A_{125}&=150,\\
\max A_{250}&=250.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d
=1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250
=499.
\]

Therefore the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}
\]
